issue.replace_path_mod_files_remain: Replacing the map leaves {count} mod files in folders the game will stop reading ({folders}); for example {example}.
explain.title.replace_path_mod_files_rem: Why: the mod already had files in {folders}
explain.outcome.replace_path_mod_files_r: With replace_path the game ignores those base-game folders but still reads the mod's: the old files would mix with the new map and point to provinces that no longer exist.
issue.forge_no_owned_provinces: No province of the new map has an owner (mode “{mode}”).
explain.title.forge_no_owned_provinces: Why: the new map has no countries
explain.outcome.forge_no_owned_provinces: The game starts, but with no playable country: it is only useful as a canvas to hand out the world by hand later.
issue.forge_orientation_suspect: {file} looks upside down compared with positions.txt ({score}% of provinces match).
explain.outcome.forge_orientation_suspec: Victoria II BMPs are stored bottom-up; an image exported by another program can end up flipped, and then each province lands where another should be.
issue.forge_not_24bit: {file} is in {mode} mode: the province map must be 24-bit RGB.
explain.outcome.forge_not_24bit: The game identifies each province by its exact colour; with a palette, an alpha channel or greyscale it cannot read the colours in definition.csv.
issue.forge_size: The map is {width}×{height}: not the base game size (5616×2160).
explain.title.forge_size: Why: the size is not the base game one
explain.outcome.forge_size: The game loads maps of other sizes if they are multiples of 8, but the camera, the minimap and some mods expect 5616×2160; padding with sea keeps the usual size.
issue.forge_color_reserved: {count} provinces use a reserved colour (such as {color}).
explain.title.forge_color_reserved: Why: some colours cannot be provinces
explain.outcome.forge_color_reserved: Pure black and pure white are used by the game for other things: a province with those colours usually vanishes from the map.
explain.title.forge_tiny_province: Why: some provinces are too small
explain.outcome.forge_tiny_province: A tiny province cannot be clicked and its name does not fit; it is usually a drawing leftover best merged into its neighbour.
issue.forge_seam_province: {count} provinces cross the east-west edge of the map.
explain.title.forge_seam_province: Why: some provinces are cut by the map edge
explain.outcome.forge_seam_province: The map wraps around: a province on both sides of the edge is one province for the game. It is not an error, but its name and capital go to one side.
issue.province_isolated: {count} provinces touch no other province (the first is {first}).
explain.outcome.province_isolated: With no neighbours it cannot be reached by land or sea: armies cannot enter and the game can fail when computing paths.
issue.forge_land_sea_unknown: It is not known which provinces are land and which are sea.
explain.title.forge_land_sea_unknown: Why: the land and sea information is missing
explain.outcome.forge_land_sea_unknown: The game needs the list of seas (sea_starts) for ships and ports; without it everything would be land. Choose where to take it from: terrain, the heightmap or default.map.
issue.forge_land_sea_ambiguous: {count} provinces have both land and water and it is unclear what they are.
explain.title.forge_land_sea_ambiguous: Why: some provinces are half land and half water
explain.outcome.forge_land_sea_ambiguous: A province is wholly land or wholly sea; if half of it is water, ships or armies will behave oddly there.
issue.terrain_not_indexed: {file} is in {mode} mode: the terrain must be 8-bit palettised.
explain.outcome.terrain_not_indexed: The game reads the number of each pixel, not its colour: without a palette it cannot tell which terrain each place is.
issue.rivers_not_indexed: {file} is in {mode} mode: the rivers must be 8-bit palettised.
explain.outcome.rivers_not_indexed: The game reads each river's width from the pixel number; without a palette, rivers are not drawn or appear as blots.
issue.terrain_index_invalid: {count} terrain pixels use numbers the game does not recognise (for example {first}).
explain.title.terrain_index_invalid: Why: there are unknown terrain numbers
explain.outcome.terrain_index_invalid: A number with no entry in terrain.txt leaves the pixel without terrain: it shows black or with the wrong texture.
issue.terrain_index_placeholder: {count} terrain pixels use a placeholder index.
explain.outcome.terrain_index_placeholde: Some programs paint with a provisional index; the game accepts it, but the terrain of those provinces will not be what you expect.
explain.outcome.rivers_diagonal: The game follows rivers along the four sides of each pixel: a diagonal jump cuts the river in two.
issue.rivers_in_water: {count} river pixels are in the sea or a lake.
explain.title.rivers_in_water: Why: there are rivers inside water
explain.outcome.rivers_in_water: A river over water is drawn on top of the sea and does nothing; it is usually a conversion leftover.
explain.title.river_source_missing: Why: some rivers have no source
explain.outcome.river_source_missing: The game draws the river anyway; the source only changes how its first segment looks.
issue.heightmap_size: The heightmap is {width}×{height} and the province map {expected_width}×{expected_height}: it will be rescaled.
explain.title.heightmap_size: Why: the heightmap has another size
explain.outcome.heightmap_size: The workshop fits the heightmap to the province map size; mountains lose some detail.
issue.forge_too_many_provinces: The map would have {count} provinces and the limit is {limit}.
explain.outcome.forge_too_many_provinces: The game stores province numbers in 16 bits: above {limit} it does not load the map.
issue.forge_edit_conflict: An edit ({edit}, step {step}) no longer fits the regenerated world: {reason}.
explain.title.forge_edit_conflict: Why: a manual edit lost its place
explain.outcome.forge_edit_conflict: When parameters changed, step {step} was recalculated and what the edit touched is gone. Discarding it is safe; if you want it, redo it on the new world.
issue.forge_env_changed: The project was saved with other numpy or Pillow versions.
explain.outcome.forge_env_changed: The saved world opens as it is; only if you regenerate steps could small differences from the other computer appear.
issue.forge_export_conflict: {file} already exists in the mod and the export will overwrite it.
explain.outcome.forge_export_conflict: You changed the file by hand after the last export (or the workshop did not make it): overwriting it loses that change, which stays in the mod's trash.
issue.forge_loc_shadowed: Another mod localisation file defines the province names first ({file}).
explain.outcome.forge_loc_shadowed: The game uses the first definition of each key it finds: the new map's names would not show.
fix.mapforge.trash_mod_files: Send those files to the mod's trash
fix.mapforge.share_existing_tags: Share the map among the existing countries
fix.mapforge.merge_reserved: Replace those colours with free ones
fix.mapforge.merge_tiny: Merge them into their longest neighbour
fix.mapforge.merge_isolated: Merge them into the nearest province
fix.mapforge.use_common_index: Use the province's most common terrain
fix.mapforge.remove_river_water: Remove the river from the water
fix.mapforge.remove_shadowed_keys: Remove those keys from the other file
